task.title: Bipartite edges: the greatest number of edges on p vertices

located_defect.description: The source concludes (stored source line 0026) that the greatest number of edges of a bipartite graph on p vertices is p^2/4. With 'bipartite' = 2-colourable (colour classes may be empty), vertices labelled by Fin p, the formula read in ℚ and 'greatest' an attained maximum (IsGreatest), this is the located defect. Supply the corrected value as a natural-number expression in p and prove that it is the greatest element of BipCounts p for every p; there is no separate target theorem beyond the corrected statement.

task.allowed_edit: Replace the hole in `max_edges` by a closed natural-number expression in p (no reference to BipCounts, edges, IsGreatest, sSup, Set, Finset, SimpleGraph; no if/match); nothing else in the fixed part may change. BipCounts p, IsGreatest (an attained maximum, not merely an upper bound) and the quantification over every p are fixed; p may not be restricted (even p, p ≥ 2, non-empty classes). Do not redefine graph, edges, BipCounts, SourceClaim or UniversalSourceClaim; no instances, notations, macros, axioms or exports.
